frozenBy: benchmark-family-paper PR A6 (issue 85), rebuilt after the independent review of PR #87 and before any probe run
engineNote: All 34 pinned artifacts depend on benchmark-core@^0.1.0; 0.1.0 is the only published version as of frozenAt. The universal submission is a Trace {answer?: string, toolLog?: ToolLogEntry[], finalState?: unknown}; the runner passes the model completion string as answer and episode fields verbatim. benchmark-core@0.1.0 itself promises no answer normalisation: exactMatch is JSON.stringify equality, regexMatch is raw, numericWithin only trims.
oracle: Defined per pinned artifact in paper/data/exp/oracle-definition.csv: the submission the package's good mock policy produces on the task. That is answer text for single-answer packages, a tool-call trace for replay packages, a file edit (write_file of src/impl.expr then submit) for exploit-resistance, and answer text plus a trace where the package grades both. A probe that edits answer text is outside contract where the oracle sends no answer text.
emptySubmission: The submission {} on the same task: no answer, no toolLog, no finalState. It is the baseline for every TYPE A attack.
contractBasis: Every honest-variant probe carries promise_source entries that cite text published inside a pinned tarball (package@version:file#line plus the quoted sentence). A probe whose transform no published artifact promises is kind unpromised-exploratory: it runs and is reported, but a drop never counts as a grader defect.

expectedRule.honest-variant: score(probe) >= score(oracle) - 0.001 on every in-scope task at every artifact where the probe applies
expectedRule.unpromised-exploratory: reported only: score(probe) relative to score(oracle) - 0.001 is recorded, never counted as a grader defect
expectedRule.attack-A: FAIL if score(probe) > score(empty submission on the same task) + 0.001
expectedRule.attack-B: FAIL if score(probe) differs from score(oracle on the same task) by more than 0.001 in either direction
